task.instruction: Find the top story from BBC News in the technology section for today.

final_answer:
The top story in BBC News' Technology section is **"Global stocks plunge as fears over US AI slowdown spread to Asia and Europe"** (published 23 hours ago, by business reporters Rachel Clun, Osmond Chia and Nick Edser).

Global stock markets tumbled as investors sold off tech shares on fears that the US midterm election results would slow the development of artificial intelligence. The sell-off began in the US and spread to Asia and Europe, wiping trillions of dollars off major tech firms' value. The tech-heavy Nasdaq sank 5.5% on Thursday, Asian markets fell heavily on Friday and European markets opened lower. Investors are worried about tougher AI regulation after Democrat candidates opposed the data centres the technology depends on — on top of existing doubts about whether the huge sums being spent on AI will pay off.

The "magnificent seven" tech companies, including Apple, Nvidia and Tesla, shed a trillion dollars in a single trading day, with Nvidia down more than 9%. Shares in Elon Musk's SpaceX and Tesla fell 8% and nearly 11% respectively, shaving over $300bn off their combined market value. The Nasdaq lost an estimated $2.5tn (£1.9tn) and is now in correction territory — at least 10% below its recent high.

Note on timing: it is the lead item on the Technology front page right now, but it is dated 23 hours ago (Friday 6 November), not today. The freshest items in the "More Tech" list are newer — "AI in property listings is false advertising, house-hunters say" (5 hrs ago) and "Villagers left without internet for weeks... again" (6 hrs ago) — and there is a follow-up, "AI stocks climb after trillions wiped from market values" (16 hrs ago).

judge.rationale: The final page shows the Technology section lead as “Global stocks plunge as fears over US AI slowdown spread to Asia and Europe,” matching the agent’s answer.
